# Kalimat Plus

> Kalimat Plus (كلمات, "words") is a free, browser-based Fusha (Modern Standard Arabic) vocabulary trainer for learners moving beyond the basics, made by Ummah Apps. It follows on from Kalimat, the beginner trainer. URL: https://kalimat-plus.ummahapps.ai/

## What it does

- 277 Fusha words and phrases in four topics:
  - Religion and worship (51): prayer, wudu, fasting, zakat, sadaqah, Hajj, Umrah, Quran, dua, dhikr, iman, taqwa, tawbah and related verbs.
  - Tarbiyyah and upbringing (95): Islamic upbringing and parenting, adab, role models (qudwah), fitrah, values, habits, encouragement and reward, discipline, rights and duties, being dutiful to parents (birr al-walidayn), and verbs such as to raise (rabba), to discipline (addaba), to advise, to encourage and to obey. It also covers bringing up children in modern times: smartphones, screens and screen time, the internet, social media, influencers, video games and addiction, peer pressure, bullying, Islamic identity, mental health, privacy, parental controls and the generation gap.
  - Relationships and character (74): friendship, trust, respect, honesty, emotions, personality traits and related verbs.
  - Environment (57): climate, global warming, pollution, recycling, energy, natural disasters, sustainability and related verbs.
- Feelings and sayings: 47 expressive words (flame, dignity, longing, imagination, to smile, to feel at ease), picked from words used in well-loved Arabic sayings.
- GCSE Arabic (Pearson Edexcel): 198 more words and phrases, in a group for each of the 13 topics of the five GCSE themes: Identity and culture; Local area, holiday and travel; School; Future aspirations, study and work; International and global dimension. Takallum has GCSE speaking phrases for the same topics.
- Every entry has full harakat (vowel marks), an English meaning, and an example sentence in Arabic with an English translation.
- Verbs show the past tense, present tense and verbal noun (masdar). Nouns show their plural, labelled as a sound or broken plural.
- Words and sentences are spoken aloud using the device's text-to-speech voice at slow, normal or natural speed.
- Games: a multiple-choice reading quiz, "say it from memory", "say the verb forms" and "say the plural".
- Progress panel: how many words are known well, the percentage, the next goal and progress in each topic.
- Progress tracking: mark words as learned and they go into the game. Get a word right 5 times in a row and it moves to Known well by itself. Known-well words come back for spaced memory checks (after 3 days, 1 week, 2 weeks, 1 month, 2 months, 4 months); a forgotten word goes back into the game.
- Learners can add their own words with plurals, verb forms and example sentences.
- Up to three learners can share one device, the same learners as in the sister apps Takallum Kids, Kalimat and Takallum.
- Free, no account, no ads. Progress is stored only in the learner's browser.

## Who it is for

Intermediate learners of Modern Standard Arabic who want to talk about ideas in Fusha: GCSE and A-level Arabic students, home-schooling families, parents learning the language of tarbiyyah, and adults in Quranic or Madinah-style Arabic classes.
